## Redact personal data from any item with a reusable sub-workflow and an audit log

### How it works
This is a tool other workflows call, not a workflow that runs on its own. Send it any item and it comes back with the personal data handled and a report of what it could not classify. There is no model in it. Emails, IBANs, payment cards, phone numbers and IP addresses are found by pattern and then checked: an IBAN must pass mod-97 and a card must pass Luhn before anything is touched, so an order number is not redacted as a card. Three modes, set in one table: mask keeps the shape, pseudonymise replaces a value with a keyed HMAC so the same input always gives the same token, and remove replaces it outright. Pseudonymise refuses to run while the key is empty rather than falling back to a plain hash, because an unkeyed hash of an email address can be reversed with a word list. The audit log records counts and detector names only, never the values, because a redactor that writes the original into a log has not redacted anything. Every answer carries its blind spots: personal names are not detected, and anything that looked like it might identify somebody is returned as an unclassified candidate rather than quietly ignored.

### Setup
1. Run Set Up And Self Test once. It creates two tables and loads the default policy.
2. Optional. Set a pseudonym_key in redaction_policy if you want pseudonymise mode.
3. That same run feeds eight known probes through the real detector and posts the result to Discord.

### Customization tips
Turn individual detectors off in redaction_policy. Adding one means adding a validator too, not just a pattern.

## 1. Create the two tables (run once)
The policy and the audit log are created with typed columns, or reused when the names already exist. [Data table node docs](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/core-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.datatable/)

## 2. Load the default policy
Set The Default Policy holds every value a user changes before the first run: the mode, the pseudonym key and one switch per detector. It is written to the policy table, which the redactor re-reads on every call.

## 3. The redactor, called by your other workflows
The [Execute Sub-workflow Trigger](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/core-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.executeworkflowtrigger/) is the entry point. Send `{ payload, requested_by }` and get the item back with a report. No model, no HTTP, no key.

## 4. Detect, validate, replace
An IBAN passes mod-97 and a card passes Luhn before anything is touched. An empty policy or a missing pseudonym key refuses rather than redacting nothing quietly.

## 5. Self test, and the log
Eight probes go through the same detector, including look-alikes that must be left alone. The log records counts and detector names, never the values.
